This is your markets briefing for Thursday, November 19. It is read by an AI-generated voice.

Our top story comes from Fictional Markets Wire.

Norland's producer prices rose 0.4 percent in October from the previous month, according to the Norland Statistics Office.

Economists had expected a smaller increase of 0.2 percent from the previous month.

Compared with October last year, Norland producer prices were up 2.6 percent.

Excluding food and energy, Norland producer prices rose 0.1 percent month-on-month.

By 15:00 local time, the Norland krone was up 0.5 percent against the euro.

Analysts at Fictional Bank said the stronger-than-expected reading made a rate cut at the central bank's December meeting less likely.
